question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite our limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{7}{4{(x-2)}^{3}}=\frac{7}{4}\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{1}{{(x-2)}^{3}}
$$

For any non-constant polynomial $P(x),$ we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \pm \infty }(\frac{1}{P(x)})=0.
$$

Therefore, since ${(x-2)}^{3}$ is a non-constant polynomial, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{1}{(x-2)^{3}}=0.
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the original limit as follows:

$$
\frac{7}{4}\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{1}{{(x-2)}^{3}}=\frac{7}{4}\cdot 0=0
$$
